```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = NA)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
# Show the instructor's project folder as "c407", as students will see it
course_root <- getwd()
default_output_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  default_output_hook(gsub(course_root, "/Users/you/c407", x, fixed = TRUE), options)
})
```

## R code runs in two places

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Console

Quick commands, checks, and package installation. Nothing is saved.
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Quarto document

Code, results, and your notes in one `.qmd` file. This is the record of your analysis.
:::
::::

::: {.key-point}
Experiment in the Console. Keep everything you want to reproduce in the document.
:::

## Use the Console for quick commands

Type and run this command in Positron's **Console**:

```{r}
#| label: console
mean(mtcars$mpg)
```

The result appears directly below the command, and it is gone when you restart R.

## A Quarto document mixes text and code

````markdown
---
title: "Sample analysis"
format: html
---

```{{r}}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
```

The table below shows the number of sales in each year.
````

::: {.small}
- **YAML header** (between the `---` lines): the title and output format.
- **Code chunk** (starts with ```` ```{r} ````): R code.
- **Chunk options** (lines starting with `#|`): a `label`, or `echo: false` to hide code.
- **Markdown**: everything else.
:::

## Create your first Quarto document

1. In Positron, choose **File → New File… → Quarto Document**.
2. Save it in the `scripts` folder as `scripts/sample_analysis.qmd`.
3. Add one setup chunk right after the YAML header, with the packages you need.

To insert a new chunk at the cursor, press:

::: {.shortcut}
**Windows/Linux:** `Ctrl + Shift + I`\
**macOS:** `Command + Shift + I`
:::

::: {.key-point}
Keep one setup chunk at the top. Every later chunk can use the packages it loads.
:::

::: {.notes}
TODO: Confirm the menu path for a new Quarto document in the current Positron release.
:::

## Run code one statement at a time

Place the cursor inside an R statement and press:

::: {.shortcut}
**Windows/Linux:** `Ctrl + Enter`\
**macOS:** `Command + Enter`
:::

Positron sends the statement to the Console, and the result appears there.

::: {.key-point}
`Enter` creates a new line. `Ctrl/Command + Enter` runs code.
:::

## Run a whole chunk

- Click **Run Cell** above the chunk, or
- place the cursor in the chunk and press `Ctrl/Command + Shift + Enter`.

```{r}
#| label: chunk
mpg_mean <- mean(mtcars$mpg)
mpg_mean
```

## Quick check: where does the code go?

**A.** Console  **B.** Quarto document

1. `install.packages("tidyverse")`
2. The code that produces the figures for your presentation
3. `?mean`, to read a help page once

::: {.notes}
Answers: 1. A (setup, not analysis). 2. B (it must be reproducible). 3. A (a one-time lookup).
:::

## The working directory is R's starting point

The working directory is the folder R uses when it reads or writes a file.

```{r}
#| label: getwd
getwd()
```

When you open the **c407** folder in Positron, it becomes the working directory.

::: {.notes}
- Positron workspaces: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## Quarto also runs your code from c407

Your `.qmd` files are in `scripts/`, but `_quarto.yml` tells Quarto to run code from the `c407` folder:

```yaml
project:
  execute-dir: project
```

::: {.key-point}
In every document, paths start from `c407`, whether you run a chunk or render the whole file.
:::

## R looks in the working directory first

Add this chunk to `sample_analysis.qmd` and run it:

```{r}
#| label: path-fail
bca <- read_rds("bca262.rds")
```

It fails because the file is inside the **data** folder, not directly in `c407`.

## A relative path starts from c407

```{r}
#| label: path-ok
bca <- read_rds("data/bca262.rds")
dim(bca)
```

::: {.path-line}
`c407` → `data` → `bca262.rds`
:::

`bca` has `r format(nrow(bca), big.mark = ",")` sales and `r ncol(bca)` columns.

## Relative paths keep working when the folder moves

- Use `/` between folders: `data/bca262.rds`.
- Relative paths are shorter than full paths such as `/Users/you/Downloads/c407/data/bca262.rds`.
- They keep working when the whole `c407` folder moves to another place or computer.

::: {.key-point}
Never use `setwd()` or full paths in course documents.
:::

## Browse before you analyse

```{r}
#| label: browse
bca |>
  select(sale_date, juris_label, act_use_name, price) |>
  head()
```

Which columns might help explain differences in sale price?

::: {.notes}
In the Console, `View(bca)` opens the full table in Positron's Data Explorer.
:::

## Calculate annual average prices

```{r}
#| label: avg-price
avg_price <- bca |>
  group_by(sale_year = year(sale_date)) |>
  summarise(avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE))

avg_price |> tail(4)
```

The last year is incomplete: the data end on `r format(max(bca$sale_date), "%d %B %Y")`.

## Plot annual average prices

```{r}
#| label: plot
#| fig-height: 3.3
avg_price_plot <- ggplot(avg_price, aes(sale_year, avg_price)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Average sale price",
       caption = "2026: January to early March only")
avg_price_plot
```

## Running and rendering are different

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Running

Uses your **current** R session. Objects you made in the Console are still there.
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Rendering

Starts a **fresh** R session and runs every chunk from top to bottom.
:::
::::

::: {.warning}
"It works when I run it but fails when I render" usually means the document uses something you created only in the Console.
:::

## Render to check that the document works

- Click **Preview** in Positron, or
- run this in the **Terminal**:

```bash
quarto render scripts/sample_analysis.qmd
```

The result is `scripts/sample_analysis.html`, with your text, code, and output.

::: {.key-point}
Render often. A document that renders from scratch is reproducible.
:::

::: {.notes}

:::

## Render a PDF report with Typst

List both formats in the YAML header:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
```yaml
format:
  html: default
  typst: default
```
:::

::: {.column width="56%"}
- Indent `html` and `typst` more than `format:`.
- Indent them by the same amount.
- Use spaces, not tabs.
:::
::::

- `quarto render scripts/sample_analysis.qmd` now makes both `sample_analysis.html` and `sample_analysis.pdf`.
- **Preview** shows the first format listed. Put `typst` first to preview the PDF.

::: {.key-point}
Typst comes with Quarto, so you do not need LaTeX (`format: pdf` needs it). PDF output is static, so use static maps (`tmap_mode("plot")`) and keep tables simple and narrow.
:::

## Save a figure to use outside Quarto

```{r}
#| label: save
#| eval: false
ggsave("temp/avg_price.png", avg_price_plot, width = 8, height = 4.5)
```

- A rendered report or Quarto slides already include the figure. You don't need a PNG.
- For PowerPoint or Google Slides, save a PNG and insert the file. Don't use screenshots.
- `width` and `height` are in inches; 8 × 4.5 fits a 16:9 slide.

::: {.key-point}
Because `ggsave()` is in the document, every render remakes the PNG, so it always matches your code.
:::

## Quick check: why did the render fail?

You ran `bca <- read_rds("data/bca262.rds")` in the Console, then wrote this chunk:

```{r}
#| label: render-fail
#| eval: false
bca |> nrow()
```

Running the chunk works, but rendering stops with `object 'bca' not found`. Why?

::: {.notes}
Answer: rendering starts a fresh R session, and `bca` was created only in the Console. Move the `read_rds()` line into the document.
:::
